documents.t: elanous graph run <file> [--dry-run] · elanous graph status <id> — walk an operations graph whose nodes run registered recipes. Release page

Tools started from the Telegram bot (such as event video) find node and Homebrew even when the bot runs as a background service. elanous harness stop accepts the short run id shown in output and stops that run's pod jobs too. Release checklist entries written by an older build to checklist.json are picked up again instead of being ignored. Creating a worktree for a large repository no longer times out after 30 seconds, and a timeout is reported clearly instead of ending at a progress line. elanous harness stop finds a run's launcher process even when the orchestrator record is missing, and says what it looked at instead of reporting «no process». elanous update --restart no longer restarts the service when the same build is already installed. Windows: elanous no longer crashes on start (a Linux-only library was loaded at import), and the PowerShell installer keeps the system PATH after installing Bun and adds elanous to the user PATH so a new window finds it. Send a business card photo to the Telegram bot and get a summary, an approach strategy and a follow-up draft back in the same chat (nothing is sent); a photo without a caption starts this only when the photo looks like a business card, and a keyword like «business card», «strategy» or «email draft» starts it right away and picks just that part. elanous seat loop --seat <SEAT> --once picks a seat's next assigned item and records what it would do (shadow by default · off unless configured), and elanous seat report summarises the day. Operational reports (schedule health, retros, memory review, repo watch) no longer fall through to a different bot's chat when no channel is mapped for them. Ask elanous where the release stands or tell it to add an item or move a release date; changes ask you once before they are made. In web app chat, an approval sheet appears before a write or shell tool runs: allow once, always allow for this session, or deny; with no answer in 60 seconds nothing runs. Drag a file onto the web app chat to see a «drop here to attach» overlay, and paste a screenshot to attach it. The web app menu is grouped into Today · Chats · Work · Create · Library · Settings. An unknown /command in web app chat is no longer sent to the model; you are told it is unknown or not yet supported in the web app. Reopening or reattaching the web terminal no longer leaves a black screen; earlier output and new output both show. In the terminal chat box, Ctrl+C clears what you typed, and pressing it twice on an empty box exits. When a pod run ends, the harness says why (stopped, supervisor verdict, left a PR) instead of claiming it never reached the pod. The steward can launch scheduled harness goals on pods in parallel under a budget gate, raising human decisions for money, publishing or security, and reporting each landing back — shadow mode first. Web app chat shows your conversations in a list on the left with «+ New chat» and search; on a phone the list opens as a drawer. The first time you run eln, it starts the engine and shows a browser setup link (and opens the browser when a display is available); elanous setup --terminal keeps setup in the terminal. «Assign to COO» in the web app: approve or hold a posting right in the request, play result videos and images in place, and see each result's sources. «Field upload» in the web app shows the event folder's count and finished reel as soon as it opens (including uploads from other devices), shows why a reel failed, and says up front which picked files are left out (over 20, over 100 MB, or over 250 MB in total). The web app sends a push notification when a request you assigned finishes, fails, or waits for your approval; tapping it opens that request. Reopening an earlier web chat shows each message at the time it was sent, not the time you opened it. On narrow screens (phones, a folded Fold) the web app's top bar shrinks to one line with the rest under «⋯», and the web terminal opens full screen on touch devices. On narrow screens the web terminal's three toolbar rows shrink to one line (terminal name · connection dot · «⋯» with every action). When an assigned document draft fails its check, elanous rewrites it once with the reviewer's note before giving up. On phones and a folded Fold, the web app has bottom tabs (Today · Chats · Work · Create · More). An assigned task that finished now shows its result in the web app even when the graph wrote its file in its own run folder or only answered in text, and a failed task shows the step's actual reason. On first run, if a phone is on the same Wi-Fi, elanous also prints a one-time link (and a QR code when available) to continue setup from the phone, and over SSH it prints the one ssh -L line to open setup from your own computer. A request sent to the Telegram bot as a directive now gets its result back in the same chat when the work finishes: the produced file, or a link and one-line summary. Settings has a «Try experimental features» switch; turn it on to see features still in beta, marked 실험 (experimental). Add 즉석 (or instant) after #현장 in a Telegram caption to get the quicker field reel that reuses pre-made intro and end cards; telegram.fieldReelMode sets the default. In the web first-run setup you can sign in with your ChatGPT subscription right there — in the browser on the same computer, or with a device code from a phone — without going back to the terminal. The web app now says 대화 (conversation) instead of 세션 (session) in the conversation picker, its ID pill and the delete dialog, and the delete dialog says plainly that it cannot be undone. In web app chat you can keep typing while a reply streams; your next messages queue as chips and send in order. Assigned tasks can now use event photos and the field feed, take attached files, and a plain question is answered by the seat instead of failing with «no installed graph fits». The one-line installer no longer stops on a fresh root Ubuntu (WSL, containers) for want of unzip, curl or git: as root with apt it installs them itself (--no-install-deps to opt out); other users still get the one-line hint. In the terminal app, messages you type while a reply is streaming now appear in the chat log when they are sent, in order. In web app chat, once you deny a write or shell tool the assistant stops asking for the same tool again in that reply, and the approval wait time can be set with acp.toolApproval.timeoutMs. In chat, a short fact question is answered from a web search with sources, instead of opening the shell and browser and running out of time. elanous nexus status no longer sends its local health check through an HTTP proxy, so it reports a running daemon correctly on machines with a proxy set. In web app chat, /sessions lists your recent conversations and /resume <first characters> picks one up again. In web app chat, /model <tier> shows or sets the model tier (unknown values are not saved), and /provider and /reasoning point you to the matching settings. The web app's Today screen shows approvals waiting for you, your five most recent requests and your five most recent conversations. Web app chat can group conversations into projects: pick a project from the switcher, or create your first one when you have none. Plus 184 internal changes.

Add a bounded context journal for Claude Code hooks, Codex agent missions, and harness child lifecycle events. Workflow runs now support single-node execution, resuming from prior runs, and pin-required test mode. Decision-card answers now resume the waiting harness run, while deadlines retain safe fallback behavior. two programs writing to the same conversation at once no longer lose messages from its count or undo its project assignment; assigning a conversation to a project that does not exist now answers «not found» (404), and the dashboard suggests a project from the session folder whenever it changes. The INSIDE2 live-event SSE endpoint (GET /v1/inside/events) streams graph, harness, seat, steward, and PTY decision updates with secret values masked. Steward live mode launches eligible goals only after pre-launch duplicate, budget and location checks, while money, publishing and security decisions still require human approval. Add a rate-limited diagnostics intake endpoint that stores doctor bundles in private S3 and returns a support code. The elanous-basics plugin now includes a Google Workspace skill for your own Gmail and Calendar, plus Drive and Sheets reads. A new elanous-essentials pack bundles five everyday skills — YouTube digests, web search and crawling, link digests, diagrams and lecture-note digitizing — each with a free path and a bring-your-own-key path. elanous harness stop <run> now finds and stops a run that was launched from another worktree: the run is bound to its process in a per-user host registry, and the stop still checks the process start time before any signal. Pod pool members can use separate registry ports, and lease checks exclude members whose in-Pod DNS lookup fails. Setup automatically enables skills for signed-in gh, gws, op, and himalaya CLIs, skips unavailable or signed-out CLIs, and keeps public GitHub repository reads available without signing in. Plugin make now researches the web and Aside local memory before drafting a connector, skill, and graph, and continues when research is unavailable. workflows can run independent nodes in parallel (concurrency, default 1) and route a failed node to an on_error handler instead of stopping. Condense a day of context events and decisions into source-linked, project-and-seat memory with correction, conflict and retirement signals. Install, list and remove YAML team sets of titled personas with validated handoffs. Pods have a lite tier (2 GiB) you opt into: elanous pod run --lite runs network-skill commands (omni-crawl, omni-digest) on a small image, and --pod-memory lite or a Pod 메모리: lite goal line gives a harness goal 2 GiB; a lite run that runs out of memory retries once on the high tier, and pod lease status shows lite slots. elanous graph variant <template> --plan <json> --dry-run|--run validates a variant, saves its graph beside the run ledger, and executes the validated wiring. The harness gate runs up to 30 reverse-import and HTTP-route consumer tests, including PWA tests for removed routes, and warns with the full overflow list. elanous make "<one-line request>" classifies the request and routes it to the existing plugin maker or workflow builder, asking which to use when classification fails. Isolate provider availability tests from host credentials and verify Codex-first selection with the default fallback chain. Plugin make can prepare a leak-checked official-market bundle after local installation, with an optional configured signature and no publishing. elanous skills install essential --code <CODE> --email <address> --agree installs the essential skill pack from a gift code — nothing is sent without --agree, existing skill folders are never overwritten, and an oversized or mismatched download is refused. Asking how X reacts to something now searches X itself, so the answer cites x.com posts. Delegated work now picks a default output for each task — a report, slides, a research doc or a post draft — instead of ending in a chat answer, and what was produced is recorded in one outputs list. Cache successful per-member DNS checks for ten minutes under a host lock and exclude labeled DNS probe Pods from goal counts. the harness launch gate no longer blocks every launch when the launch universe's config has no model chain: it judges with the built-in default chain and prints a warning, and an explicit --child-llm-provider counts as the chain. classification calls no longer fail when no global LLM provider is configured: a role that names its own provider resolves without one, and an injected classifier transport still runs (marked unresolved). Plus 206 internal changes.

elanous release checklist add warns about an ID used in another release and requires --allow-duplicate-id to proceed; a blocked move now identifies the destination cell. CLI and cron outbound sends now register a standalone log-store sink, recording bot identity, kind, source, delivery path, outcome and body length without message text or credentials. elanous persona add <name> --from <preset> creates one editable YAML persona; persona edit --set validates fields and returns exit 2 with a one-line reason for unknown keys. Harness ask/say launch gates now have an isolated real-CLI test for duplicate blocking, budget blocking, and force overrides, while unknown active-run lookups record their reasons. Harness launches warn and proceed when provider usage is unmeasured; only measured exhaustion blocks the launch. When a change has more than 30 caller tests, the gate keeps the ones closest to it — tests naming a route on a changed line, then direct importers nearest in the directory tree — instead of the alphabetically first; the overflow still runs in the release-cut sweep. Retry a silent release-gate Pod shard once in a fresh Pod before reporting it stalled. the release loop now packs the internal ops feed from the release tag (a fresh checkout with the web UI built), so operations hosts receive exactly the released code instead of whatever main held at that moment. Harness runs and external agent missions publish fail-soft claimed and done events with run and PR references to the context journal. Market review bundles exclude plugin runtime and graph-run state while retaining the private-content leak gate for authored files. Persist ordered agent-mission PTY decisions to logs.db so the PWA inside scene can replay them. when a harness change edits a test, the gate again also runs the changed sources' co-located and related tests (a narrowing that ran only the edited test is reverted). Plus 81 internal changes.
Security hardening for the local daemon, a simpler rule for which environment a command runs in, web setup for chat bots, and a lighter, safer install.

curl -fsSL https://github.com/ElanvitalAI/elanous/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash # one line npm had not been updated for 0.2.2; the one-line installer above is the way to install this release.

The daemon no longer hands out its admin token over HTTP. connect-info returns no token; a new device pastes its token once. Every /v1 route now requires authentication by default. Previously a few read routes (including the notes vault search) and several settings/control writes could be reached without a token. Telegram and Discord bot tokens are stored once, in the secrets store, and referenced from config — no more plaintext tokens in config.json. Isolated (test) environments no longer receive copies of production secrets: plaintext secret fields are stripped, outbound credentials (chat bot tokens, web-push keys) are left out of the copied secrets file, and copies are written 0600. elanous doctor reports configuration and secret files that other users could read, and elanous doctor --fix --yes tightens them (the folder to 700, files lose group/other bits; nothing is read).

Which environment am I in? The rule is now: an explicit root (--test, --config-dir, ELANOUS_STATE_DIR) wins; otherwise the installed copy is production and any source checkout is an isolated environment. The old "leader tree" setting is gone. elanous where shows the answer and why. Web setup — connect Telegram and Discord bots from the web app (token check, secrets store, allowed users), pick the Obsidian vault and skills, and choose the answer depth. A device that is not yet connected now says so once instead of failing silently. Install and update — installing or updating from a source checkout builds the web app first and stops if the build fails, so the installed web app always matches the code. Test daemons never take production ports. A test daemon started without --port leases a port from the test band; production ports are never chosen. Resource coordinator (preview) — elanous control serve runs a small coordinator that answers "where is this resource running?" (elanous resources list|where), bound to loopback or a tailnet address, with per-machine scoped tokens. Codex accounts — the shared default account is used only up to 60% by default (a stricter global threshold still wins), and rotation moves to the next account with room. Intake — a daily intake pipeline collects items (videos, saved Telegram messages, trending GitHub repositories), queues them with a daily cap, and absorbs them into notes. Many fixes found by installing on bare Ubuntu 26.04 and macOS machines.
If you set dashboard.uiMode or used --rich, they still load without error; the terminal UI is being simplified to a single essential layout in upcoming releases.
A shorter command (eln), a web app tab to approve and merge, tasks from Linear and other tools, several machines working as one, and a lighter terminal UI.

curl -fsSL https://github.com/ElanvitalAI/elanous/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash # one line npm had not been updated for 0.2.3; the one-line installer above is the way to install this release.

Tailnet devices paste a token once. Header-based same-origin trust now applies only to the browser on the daemon's own machine (a direct loopback connection with no proxy in front). A phone or laptop that opens the web app through the tailnet link pastes its token once; the "not connected" banner names the exact setting. Short command eln. eln is installed next to elanous; the old mda alias is gone. An existing eln that is not ours is never overwritten. elanous schedule migrate|adopt|release|delete show what they would do by default. Add --yes to apply. elanous task / elanous tasks manage the task manager's tasks (list · show · approve) instead of printing a retirement notice. Tasks from outside wait for your approval. Tasks that arrive from Linear, a webhook or another agent are queued as waiting; rules under tox.external.autoRun can run some automatically. Harness runs on Kubernetes pods merge only after the same checks pass on the host machine, so a change that is green only on Linux no longer reaches main. A run stopped by a provider, quota or credential problem keeps its branch and does not open a draft pull request. Saved Telegram links — up to 30 more a day are absorbed, separately from the daily cap of 10. Obsidian — when no vault is configured, elanous looks in ~/Documents/Obsidian. The web app can merge. The new Approvals tab has a merge button; it works only with the owner token. The terminal UI is one essential layout. The rich layout, virtual windows and their commands and tools are gone. A config that still sets dashboard.uiMode loads without error.

Approvals tab in the web app (after Intake): the summary, files and checks of a pull request waiting for approval, a direct link /approvals?pr=<n>, and approve-and-merge. On an installed copy, set the repository once: elanous config set intake.approvals.repo <owner>/<name>. Tasks from other tools — a Linear connector (elanous connector linear set-key | sync | set-webhook-secret; the Basic plan is enough), an intake endpoint POST /v1/tasks, and elanous tasks list · show · approve. An approved [dev] task runs through the harness; other tasks go to an agent with tools. See Tasks and intake. Several machines — give each machine an id, the duties it takes and its rank for a seat (elanous machine set | show); hand the coordinator seat over or let a lower-ranked machine take it when the holder stops (elanous role handoff | accept | watch | status); machines without a daemon join as light members. See Multi-machine setup. Other agents can use elanous — an MCP tool elanous_task_submit, running an elanous agent over MCP and collecting its result, and each ACP session's own working folder. A Claude Code plugin is included as a preview (claude --plugin-dir integrations/elanous-agent). Web terminal — open an agent's terminal from a link (elanous agent-mission prints it on its first lines; harness runs print a [surface-link] line), a single input path, and reopening a terminal id attaches to the live shell instead of starting another one. Web chat — the first message is no longer lost when a session is adopted, slash commands run on Enter, and controls that did nothing are gone. Intake — one box in the web app with a live preview of how the text is read; the same classifier on every surface; a Telegram link saved as a note is marked absorbed so the daily run does not absorb it again. Costs — one-off model calls (classification, summaries) are recorded with a role; elanous usage runs --by role. Workflows — webhook signature checks (auth: hmac) and a task node that files a task. Harness — elanous harness stop <runId> stops a run's process and its pod jobs; --pod-memory high gives a pod run more memory (goals that touch the web app get it automatically). Agent missions — elanous agent-mission capabilities shows each coding CLI's MCP servers, connectors and login state; when you take over the terminal, the mission waits instead of stopping. Skills — omni-digest (summarise a link, post or file) ships with elanous. It needs an xAI API key; describing images and video frames also needs AWS_S3_BUCKET. Voice — the free voice fallback uses only programs that are installed (edge-tts, macOS say).
The MCP endpoint no longer trusts a loopback connection that came through a proxy (for example tailscale serve). See the tailnet token change above.
New and updated pages: Multi-machine setup, Tasks and intake, Recommended programs, Web app, Terminal, Chat, Graph engineering.

PTY intelligence reaches stage two: elanous works inside Codex and Claude Code, installs a plugin from an agent's own menu, and passes one mission along several agents. PTY intelligence, stage two — elanous now works inside the coding agents' own screens. It opens Codex or Claude Code as a real terminal app, answers the folder-trust prompt, types the mission and submits it, watches the screen, and hands the work along a chain — Codex implements, Claude Code reviews, Codex addresses the review, elanous checks the evidence and commits. It can also open an agent's plugin menu, search, check the marketplace name and install a plugin there. You can watch every driven terminal side by side in the web app and take over at any time. See PTY intelligence. Beta — Elanous is provided as is (Apache-2.0) until the stable release. Get stable release news at elanous.ai. Docs: docs.elanous.ai · Source: ElanvitalAI/elanous

elanous agent-mission mission --backend codex --chain codex,claude,codex,elanous … — one mission handed along agents; each hand-off carries the diff or summary, and the last step commits only after the evidence check passes. --plugin <plugin>@<marketplace> — installs the plugin from inside the agent's own /plugins menu (search → marketplace name check → install), then sends the mission. Folder-trust prompts (Codex and Claude Code) are answered on a new worktree, including a prompt that appears late.

Stage one — elanous drives terminals itself. It checks the machine first, picks the smallest tool that can do the job (a shell one-liner before a coding agent), installs a missing tool by typing the package-manager line and proving it with a real command, reads an unfamiliar tool's official install page before choosing a safe line, clicks and scrolls in terminal apps that turn on mouse mode, and hands any sudo or sign-in step to you. See PTY intelligence. elanous env profile — what this machine has (OS, shell, package managers, CLIs, sign-in yes/no), read only. elanous agent-mission plan "<mission>" — which rung of the tool ladder a mission starts on, without running anything. elanous research "<query>" — several search engines at once, with the fan-out shown as it happens. elanous agent-mission install-from-docs <tool> --smoke "<cmd>" [--dry-run] — find the official install page, read it, pick a line this machine can run, install and verify. sudo lines and pages without a safe line go to you. elanous pty mouse <ref> <col> <row> — click or scroll in a mouse-enabled terminal app; refused when the app has not turned mouse mode on. Missing CLIs (jq, gh, rg, ffmpeg, node, codex) are installed by typing in the shell and checked with the smallest real job. The web app's Terminal shows each driven terminal side by side with a strip of what elanous just did and why; you can take over with the keyboard or mouse. On a credit policy, the hourly limit alert adds up the credits across your Codex accounts and their combined burn rate, and says when they will run out.
Plus 326 internal changes.

0.2.5 ships with a few known issues. None of them affect installing, starting or updating Elanous, running the harness, or your data. Fixes are planned for 0.2.6. Sub-agents reuse the prompt cache less often than in 0.2.4, so they may use slightly more tokens. Some elanous control commands show an unclear message and exit code on a machine that has not joined a control plane. Some log lines can appear twice. A few internal checks in our own test suite fail in this release. They do not change how Elanous behaves.

elanous plugin make "<request>" writes a local graph plugin from one sentence, checks its shape, installs it and can run it right away (--run). The terminal dashboard now tells you when Elanous was updated underneath it and asks you to restart it. Nodes from installed plugins now appear in the web workflow editor's palette without restarting the daemon, even when no MCP server is configured.

Running several elanous ask commands at the same time no longer fails or loses sessions from the session list. elanous ask --json prints only JSON on standard output, including on machines where no notification channel is set up. elanous harness stop finds a run's launcher process even when the orchestrator record is missing, and says what it looked at instead of reporting «no process». Plus 75 internal changes.

0.2.6 ships with a few known issues. None of them affect installing with the one-line installer, starting or updating Elanous, running the harness, or your data. Fixes are planned for the next release. If you install with npm i -g elanous, install Bun first — on a machine without Bun the elanous command cannot start in this release. The one-line installer is not affected; it sets up Bun for you. Two more marketer plugins, card-followup and video-explainer, are not in the official market yet. They will be listed in a follow-up update. A few internal checks in our own test suite fail in this release. They do not change how Elanous behaves.
Plus 296 internal changes.
When something is in the way, Elanous now tells you why and fixes what it can, right there.
curl -fsSL https://github.com/ElanvitalAI/elanous/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash # one line or npm install -g elanous.

Unreadable skills no longer stop the first screen. If a skill file from another tool can't be read, you see "N skills could not be read". After you confirm, Elanous repairs only what it can and keeps the original. Clear sign-in where a browser can't open. Over ssh or on a machine without a screen, Elanous no longer tries to open a browser; it says why and what to do instead. At the machine itself, ChatGPT sign-in opens in the browser directly. One language. First-run setup and sign-in text now use one language. elanous doctor finds local LLMs on this machine, such as Ollama and LM Studio. elanous doctor --bundle writes one diagnostics file with secrets redacted, which you can send when asking for help. Bring over what you already use. elanous import shows the skills and MCP servers it found in agents you already use, such as Claude Code and Codex. elanous import --apply brings them in. Skills stay where they are and are not copied; MCP servers arrive switched off. elanous import --undo reverts the import in one step. Secrets and sign-ins are not moved. elanous connect claude hooks up the skills of an agent you already use in one step. Telegram and Discord bots carry over. First-run setup finds your existing Telegram and Discord bot settings and shows them. It brings them over only if you agree, and token values are never shown. Decisions in your DMs. When Elanous needs a person to decide, it asks with button cards in a Telegram or Discord DM. It asks twice before anything that can't be undone. Web terminal. Opening a terminal in the web app no longer freezes for a few seconds the first time, and tabs in the background stop refreshing. Error reports. When an error happens, Elanous sends only the error, the version and a random install ID to the operators. It sends no name or email. Reports are deleted automatically after 30 days. You are told on first run. One line turns it off: elanous config set errorReports.enabled false. Docs now mark each screen as stable or experimental. A new guide shows how to put a single HTML page online with Vercel.

After you upload event photos and the vertical video is made, an Instagram feed draft is prepared on its own and waits in "Pending posts". Nothing is posted until a person taps "Final post". Plus 92 internal changes.
Smoother in the hand: a focus mode for the web terminal, a clearer terminal UI, and alerts when the Telegram bot cannot start.
curl -fsSL https://github.com/ElanvitalAI/elanous/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash # one line or npm install -g elanous.

Web terminal focus mode. Press ⤢ or Ctrl/⌘+Shift+F to fill the screen with just the terminal. Bluetooth keyboards. When a hardware keyboard is attached, the on-screen extra-key row folds away on its own. First input sooner. A new web terminal now accepts its first input much sooner; the longest wait drops from 20 seconds to 2. Terminal UI first screen shows the web app address on one line. Command palette is ordered by what you use most, with Korean descriptions. Finished turns read "Done" or "Stopped". /remaining shows each account's remaining usage and when it refills, on one line. /provider lists the models you actually use. Install banner no longer covers the chat box. The «Add to Home screen» banner now sits below the chat input instead of on top of it, on phones and desktops. Telegram bot alerts. If the Telegram bot fails to start repeatedly, you get an alert that says why.
In the web app, Library › Obsidian notes opens your vault as a folder tree you can fold. Plus internal changes to the release loop and test gate.

Voice runs on the same Discord bot you chat with in text. Set it up once: elanous onboarding discord The wizard shows where to create the bot in the Discord developer portal (copy its token, turn on the Message Content Intent, invite it to your server), then asks for the bot token, the Discord user IDs allowed to talk to it (discord.allowedUsers) and an optional home channel for scheduled messages. It saves them to your config (discord.botToken, discord.enabled). The bot then answers in servers and DMs whenever the daemon runs.

Discord now has two different voice-capable surfaces: text channel / DM voice attachments live voice channel round-trip The live voice-channel path is configured from voice.discord.voiceChannel in the active config (elanous config path, normally ~/.elanous/config.json): { "voice": { "discord": { "voiceChannel": { "enabled": true, "listenFilter": "caller", "leaveOnEmpty": true } } } } Recommended behavior: enabled = true enables the live voice-channel surface listenFilter = "caller" keeps the showroom flow single-speaker by default leaveOnEmpty = true auto-leaves when the caller exits Discord runs inside the NEXUS daemon — it starts automatically when Discord is configured: elanous nexus run For a standalone test session (same app and token, scoped to discord.testChannel.channelId, isolated state, the live daemon untouched): elanous discord-test In Discord: Join a voice channel. In a text channel on the same server, send /voice-join <voice-channel-id>. Speak normally. Use /voice-leave to exit. Notes: The command channel becomes the transcript mirror target. Recent attachment-bearing messages in that same command channel become the sticky context source for subsequent voice turns. Discord keeps text output load-bearing: 👂 Listening…, 🎙️ User: ..., 🤖 ... Voice turns are tagged before entering the ACP runner so the shared chat history keeps guild / voice channel / speaker / filter context. ELANOUS_DISCORD_VOICE_CHANNEL, ELANOUS_DISCORD_VOICE_LISTEN_FILTER, and ELANOUS_DISCORD_VOICE_LEAVE_ON_EMPTY still work as backward-compatible fallbacks, but user-config is preferred.
elanous ships a web dashboard — the PWA — next to the terminal UI. The package already contains the built web app, so there is nothing to build.

elanous nexus run # start the daemon; the web app is served with it elanous nexus show # print the web app, REST and event-stream links Open the link that nexus show prints in any browser on the same machine. The port is picked when the daemon starts (usually 31415, or the next free one if that is taken), so use the printed link rather than a fixed number. Stop a daemon you started by hand with elanous nexus stop.

Status comes from one maturity table that every surface reads. Stable screens are shown to everyone. Experimental and Tool screens are hidden until you set the screen role to Contributor in Setup (/setup → screen role); Operator screens are for the person who runs the machine (Owner). Experimental screens work, but their layout and behaviour may still change. Menu Status What it does Chat Stable Talk to elanous with streaming replies, pick a session, a backend and a surface, and see the running budget. Voice input is available where the browser allows microphone access. See Chat. Terminal Stable Live terminals from your machine in the browser — several tabs, a modifier-key bar for touch keyboards, file and camera attachments, a mirror of the terminal UI, and a live view of an agent's terminal from a link. See Terminal. Intake Experimental Since 0.2.3. One box for anything you want elanous to take — a link, a memo, a list or an instruction. It shows as you type how it reads the text, then you absorb it into your notes or send it to the harness. See Tasks and intake. Approvals Tool Things waiting for you: loop steps that ask a person before they go on, and pull requests held for your approval — each with its summary, changed files and checks. Approve, and the pull request is merged. Live Stable Your harness runs as they happen — stage bars, a stream of decisions (what, why, where to), gauges and the raw log. Everyday mode costs almost nothing; Full show records more and animates it, and switches itself off after 30 minutes. See Live. Trace Experimental Follow one run from the whole fleet down to a single decision and the log line behind it. Filters stack up as a lens you can peel back one chip at a time, and the address keeps the view so you can share it. See Trace. Missions Experimental Mission lineage and the task board in one menu; you can also hand a new goal from here. Design Tool Pick a design system, see drafts, or derive one from a URL. See Design systems. Vault Experimental Browse your Obsidian vault, read and edit notes, create new ones, and explore tags and the link graph. See Vault. 마켓 (Market) Stable Browse the signed plugin marketplaces, read a plugin's capabilities, install and remove plugins. See Plugins. Schedules Operator Every scheduled job in one list — cron, the background service and loop triggers. Settings Experimental (always shown) Models and tiers, voice and text-to-speech, persona, notifications, theme and daemon health. Setup (/setup) Stable First-time setup in the browser. Today it covers the LLM provider; the other wizard steps still run in the terminal with elanous onboarding.

Share the web app over your Tailscale network: elanous nexus pwa share enable elanous nexus pwa share status Other devices on the same tailnet can then open the link that elanous nexus show prints. Every device on your tailnet can reach it, so only share on a tailnet you trust. Turn it off with elanous nexus pwa share disable.

Since 0.2.3 From 0.2.3, a device that opens the web app through the tailnet link needs a token once. The browser on the daemon's own machine (localhost) does not. A device that is not connected yet shows a banner saying it is not connected to the daemon (인증 필요 — authentication needed). To connect it: On a device that already works, open Settings › Connect token (other devices) and press Generate connect token, then copy it. On the new device, open Settings › Daemon and paste it into Bearer token. The token is kept in that browser, so you do this once per browser. If the link stops working from another device, check elanous nexus pwa share status and run elanous nexus pwa share enable again.

The page does not load — run elanous nexus show; if no daemon is listed, start one with elanous nexus run. Something is missing after an update — first run elanous nexus restart-needed. It only reports; it restarts nothing. Restart the daemon only when it says a restart is needed. Run elanous doctor to check credentials and setup.

The Chat menu of the web app is a conversation with elanous. Replies stream in as they are written, and you can attach photos and files or talk to it with your voice. The menu's labels are partly in Korean today, so this page gives each label as it appears on screen, with the meaning in brackets.

Item What it does sess: The current session. Click the id to copy it. Double-click the new-chat button to start an empty session; the old one stays in the session list. The menu next to it (세션 메뉴 — session menu) starts a new chat or shows the session id and message count. 이번 달 $… (this month) What elanous has spent this month, and the share of your budget when a budget is set. It turns to a warning colour when you pass your notify threshold. It reads budget — when the daemon cannot report it. Microphone cost What voice input and read-aloud have cost this month. 음성 대기 (voice waiting) Voice status. The voice controls turn listening, spoken replies and the voice panel on or off.

Type in the box at the bottom and press Enter to send. Shift+Enter starts a new line. Buttons next to the box: attach a photo (camera or file), attach files, save a photo as a note (it becomes a Markdown note), and a voice memo — hold it down to record; the memo goes to intake. The chip next to the box (for example OpenAI Codex) shows which LLM provider elanous answers with. Click it to cycle through the providers you have set up. This changes elanous's own setting, so every conversation — not just this one — uses the new provider.

Lines that start with : are handled in the browser, not sent to the model. Type :help (or /help) to list them. Typing / at the start of the box opens the same list as a menu: Command What it does :session Show the current session id. :fork Start a fresh session id. :budget Show this month's spend and the notify threshold. :history [N] Summarise the last N messages on screen (default 10). :clear Clear the messages on screen.
The spend reads «budget —» — the daemon could not report it; it tries again every minute. The page does not load at all — see The web app (PWA).

The Live menu of the web app shows your harness runs as they happen: which stage each run is in, what it decided, why, and where it sent the work next. Everything on the page comes from what elanous has actually recorded; there is no demo data. The page's labels are in Korean today, so this page gives each label as it appears on screen, for example 런 (Runs).

Gauges across the top: Gauge What it counts LIVE Runs in progress DECISIONS/MIN Decisions per minute in the time window SHIPPED Pull requests opened or merged SELF-HEAL Share of runs that hit a problem and went through a repair round BURN Model tokens per minute BLOCKED Runs that are stuck 런 (Runs): one row per run in the time window. Each row is a bar of six stages: 저작 (writing the goal), 분해 (splitting it into pieces), 구현 (implementing), 게이트 (checks), 리뷰 (unattended review) and 착지 (merging). A stage lights up when the run reaches it and turns red when something fails there. Click a row to open that run's drawer: its screen and log lines, Trace 로 → (open it in Trace), MAX 이 런만 (Full show for this run only), ⏹ 멈춤 (stop, after one confirmation) and, when it waits for you, 승인 카드로 → (to its approval card). Click the row again, or ✕, to close it. 판단 스트림 (Decision stream): one line per decision, newest first, tagged with its kind: Kind Meaning Example PLAN Planning The goal was split into pieces ROUTE Sending work somewhere Switched to the next account; sent a piece to a worker machine; refused a write outside the sandbox VERIFY Checking Gates passed; review verdict HEAL Repairing Gate failed, repair round started ESCALATE Asking you The run stopped for a human decision SHIP Landing Pull request opened or merged 모델 성적표 (Model scorecard) and 리뷰 판정 (Review verdicts) summarize which models answered and how reviews went. 흐르는 로그 (Scrolling log) shows the raw signals behind it all. 빈 칸 표 (Missing fields) lists decisions whose log line has no reason or destination yet, so you can see what elanous does not record. At the bottom the page names its sources (the log and the harness run records) and refreshes every 5 seconds. Anything that looks like a secret is masked.

시간 창 (Time window): how far back to look. 신호 출처 (Signal source): which elanous instance to read. 이 인스턴스 (this instance) is the default; 전체(연합 · 최근 24시간에 쓰인 우주) (all — every instance written to in the last 24 hours) reads them together, and an isolated test instance appears here too. 공개 캡처 (Recording mode): for screenshots and recordings. It replaces account names with account-N, hides credits and dollar amounts, and masks home-folder paths and machine names. ?capture=public in the address turns it on too. 화려함 MAX (Full show): see below.

By default the page shows the summary signals elanous always records. That costs almost nothing, so you can leave the tab open. 화려함 MAX (Full show) is for demos, recordings and digging into one strange run. It adds motion to the page, and it asks the harness to record more: for every decision, why it was made, what for, and where the work went. Recording that costs something, so: The page asks first and shows how many signals per minute it is receiving right now. You choose 전체로 켜기 (turn on for all runs) or 이 런만 켜기 (only this run — pick a run first). It switches itself off after 30 minutes. While it is on, a line under the header shows the scope, the signals per minute, the payload size and the minutes left. The switch lives on the server, so every device you open sees the same state. Turn it off with 화려함 MAX 켜짐 · 끄기. If your system asks for reduced motion, Full show keeps the extra detail but drops the animation.

신호를 못 읽었다 (could not read the signals): the web app cannot reach the daemon's log. Check that the daemon is running (elanous nexus status). MAX 스위치를 못 바꿨다 (could not change the switch): usually the daemon rejected the request; sign in again or reload. An empty 런 list means no run started in the time window. Widen the window, or start one with elanous harness say "<one sentence>".

The Terminal menu of the web app opens real shells on the machine that runs the elanous daemon. You can keep several open, use them from a phone or tablet, attach files, and talk to an agent about what is on screen. The menu's labels are partly in Korean today, so this page gives each label as it appears on screen, with the meaning in brackets. The shell runs on the daemon's machine, as your user, in the folder the daemon was started from. Anything you type there runs for real.

+ at the top opens a new terminal. Each one gets a tab with its name; × or 끝내기 (end) closes it. The status at the top right shows how many terminals are open and whether they are alive. The bar under the tabs switches between three views: 터미널 (terminal) — your shells. 🖥 TUI 관측 (watch the TUI) — a read-only live view of the elanous terminal UI running in another window on the daemon's machine. PTY 목록 (PTY list) — every terminal the daemon knows about, with its history. ▦ 나란히 (side by side) shows up to three live terminals next to each other — agent terminals first. Each pane names its agent and has a strip with what elanous just did there and why. Pick the panes from the chips at the top; the address keeps your choice (?wall=<id>,<id>), so you can share the view. The connection status (ACP: 연결됨 — connected) is shown in the corner of the terminal. From 0.2.2, keys you type while it still says 연결 중 (connecting) are held and sent in order once it connects. In earlier versions, wait for 연결됨 before you type — keys typed while connecting can be lost.

On a touch screen a key bar appears under the terminal with Esc, Tab, the arrow keys and sticky Ctrl and Alt — tap Ctrl, then a letter, to send Ctrl+letter. A modifier releases itself after a few seconds if you do not use it.
documents.s: Type on a phone or tablet

documents.t: Button What it does clear Clears the screen in this browser. The shell itself keeps running as it was. Camera Takes a photo (or picks one) and puts its file path into the terminal. File Attaches one or more files and puts their paths into the terminal. You can also drag files onto the terminal. Live Shares your camera with the agent while it is on. voice→stdin Speak, and the words are typed into the terminal. record Records the terminal session on the daemon.

Under the terminal is a chat box tied to the current terminal: Plain text asks an agent about the terminal — it can see what is on screen. Lines that start with : stay local. Type :help to list them; for example :tab next, :tab prev, :cwd and :capture. It shows the session and what the agent has cost this month.

Open the same terminal on another device (see The web app (PWA)) and both see the same screen. A badge shows how many devices are attached, and a short "typing" flash appears when someone else types. Reopening a terminal tab — after a browser restart, or from another browser — returns you to the same shell that is still running; it does not start a new one.

Since 0.2.3 When elanous drives a coding CLI (codex, Claude Code, grok) in a terminal of its own, it prints a link to that terminal as soon as the terminal starts: elanous agent-mission prints [agent-mission] pty=<id> watch=<link> on its first lines, and the finished result carries the same link. A harness run prints a [surface-link] url=<link> progress line. A harness run started from Telegram also sends the link to that chat once. The link has the form https://<your-tailnet-name>/app/term/?pty=<id> and works on your tailnet only. Opening it shows that terminal's screen live, refreshed about once a second, with the terminal id at the top: It starts 읽기 전용 (read-only) — you watch; your keys go nowhere. takeover lets you type into it (the label changes to 입력 가능 — typing enabled). release gives control back. 닫기 (close) returns to your own terminals. Picking a row in PTY 목록 (PTY list) opens the same live view. When the terminal ends the view stops with «PTY 가 끝났습니다» (the PTY has ended). «소유 프로세스에 닿지 않습니다» (the owning process cannot be reached) means the process that runs it stopped answering.
documents.s: Watch an agent's terminal from a link

documents.t: The page stays on «터미널 이름을 준비하는 중…» (preparing the terminal name) — reload the page. Keys go missing right after opening (before 0.2.2) — wait until the status says ACP: 연결됨 (connected), then type. The page does not load at all — see The web app (PWA).

Experimental. This screen is hidden by default. Set the screen role to Contributor in Setup (/setup → screen role) to show it. It works, but its layout and behaviour may still change. Live is the stage: everything that is happening, at a glance. Trace is the workbench next to it. You start from every run on every machine, narrow the view step by step, and end at a single decision and the exact log line behind it — with a command you can paste into a terminal to find that line again. Trace reads the same data as Live (the log and the harness run records), so it never shows anything elanous did not record. It refreshes every 5 seconds. The page's labels are in Korean today, so this page gives each label as it appears on screen, for example 런 (Run).
documents.s: Trace (follow a run to the log line)

documents.t: Trace has four levels. The buttons at the top switch between them; a level you cannot reach yet (no run or decision picked) is greyed out. Level Button What you see L0 L0 플릿 (Fleet) Every elanous instance ("universe") that wrote signals in the time window, with its runs around it L1 L1 런 (Runs) The runs that match your lens, linked to the run that started them. The list is counted by the daemon across every instance, so quiet runs are not crowded out by busy ones. This is where the page opens L2 L2 런 한 개 (One run) One run: its stage bar, a timeline of when each stage was busy, its chain of decisions and its raw signals L3 L3 판단 (Decision) One decision from that run, with its evidence underneath (L4) Double-click a node in the graph to go one level down. Press Esc to go one level up.

Every filter you add stacks up in a row of chips under the header, starting with 렌즈 › (Lens). For example: 렌즈 › 시간: 10:20–10:45 · 우주: pod-worker · 상태: 막힘 · 런: 3a7a5625 Click a chip to remove just that filter; the others stay. When nothing is filtered the row says 전체 (all). Next to it, a counter shows how many signals, runs and universes are in view, and warns 조회 상한에 닿음 when the query hit its size limit — widen the lens carefully, because some signals were not loaded. Filters you can add: Status chips — 도는 (running), 착지 (landed: the run reached the merge stage), 막힘 (blocked) and 끊김·결과 모름 (gone quiet, result unknown). A run's status comes from the harness run records when they know it; otherwise a run that sent a signal in the last 15 minutes counts as running, and an older one as gone quiet — elanous does not call a run "running" just because nobody recorded how it ended. The number on each chip is how many runs would be left if you pressed it. Universe chips — one per instance, busiest first. Search (press /) — matches part of a run ID, a pull request number or a universe name. Time — drag across the timeline under the graph to keep only runs active in that stretch. 시간 창 (Time window) — 1, 6 or 24 hours back (24 hours by default). 신호 출처 (Signal source) — 전체(연합) (all instances, the default) or 이 인스턴스 (this instance only).
Click a node to select it; only its direct neighbours stay bright. Double-click to go one level down into it. Drag a node to pin it in place; click it twice to release it. Scroll to zoom.

The run's six stages sit in a bar — 저작 (writing the goal), 분해 (splitting it), 구현 (implementing), 게이트 (checks), 리뷰 (review) and 착지 (merging) — lit when reached and red where something failed. Below it: a timeline of when each stage first and last sent a signal; the decision chain, oldest first, one card per decision with its kind (PLAN, ROUTE, VERIFY, HEAL, ESCALATE, SHIP) and its reason; the run's raw signals, newest first. The chain's heading shows where it came from: 원천: 서버 /v1/trace (green) means the daemon gathered the run's decisions across every instance, with pull request and commit attached; 원천: 이 창 조회 · … means the page fell back to its own time-window query and says why (for example an older daemon). If the chain looks short on the fallback, widen the time window. Click a decision card to open it at L3. If a card's reason reads 계측 없음 (not recorded), elanous did not record that field for this decision. That is information, not an error: it shows you what the harness does not yet explain. To fill in the reasons for one run, turn on Full show for that run in Live (화려함 MAX → 이 런만 켜기).

The decision card shows: Field Meaning 무엇 (What) What was decided 왜 (Why) The reason recorded with it 목적 (Purpose) What it was for 어디로 (Where to) Where the work went next PATHS How many options it weighed, when recorded Use ← and → (on screen or on the keyboard) to step to the previous or next decision in the same run. Under the card, L4 증거 (evidence) shows: 원 로그 줄 (the source log line) — the exact record the card was built from. 서버 원문(비밀 가림) means it was fetched from the daemon by the line's key, with anything that looks like a secret masked, and it does not depend on the page's query limit; 이 창 조회 means it came from the page's own window. 앞뒤 1분 — up to 20 other signals from the same run, one minute either side. A command to find it again, with a copy button. It looks like: elanous logs --category harness.decision --since 2026-09-28T01:20:00.000Z --until 2026-09-28T01:22:00.000Z --grep run-3a7a5625-… --json --json-data The times are in UTC. If the run lives on another instance, the command includes --instance <name>. When the decision records a commit, its short hash; when it names a pull request, a link to its card in Approvals. If the source line is missing ("이 창의 조회에 원 줄이 없다"), the page is on its fallback and the query limit cut the line off or it belongs to another universe — narrow the time window or switch the signal source to 전체(연합).

Everything you set is kept in the address, for example /trace?level=L3&run=run-3a7a5625-…&dec=4. Send the link and the other person opens the same view on the same data. From Live, open a run and click Trace 로 → to land on that run at L2. 무대로(Live) → goes back.
Key Action / Search Esc Up one level (or leave the search box) [ / ] Up one level / from Fleet to Runs ← / → Previous / next decision (L3)

Connect to a NEXUS daemon to trace runs: the web app is not connected to a daemon. Check elanous nexus status. 이 렌즈에 런이 없다 (no runs in this lens): remove chips from the lens row one at a time. 이 창에 런 … 가 없다 (the run is not in this window): the link points at a run older than the time window, or on another instance — widen the window or choose 전체(연합).

Experimental. This screen is hidden by default. Set the screen role to Contributor in Setup (/setup → screen role) to show it. It works, but its layout and behaviour may still change. The Vault menu of the web app opens your Obsidian vault. You can browse it, search it, read and edit notes, create new ones, and explore tags and links. Changes are written straight to the Markdown files in your vault, so Obsidian sees them too. The menu's labels are in Korean today, so this page gives each label as it appears on screen, for example 태그 (Tags).

elanous needs to know where your vault is. If the Vault menu says it cannot find the vault (Obsidian vault를 찾을 수 없습니다), set the folder once — either in the web app or in the terminal: Web app: open Settings, find the Obsidian & Skills card and fill in Obsidian vault path. The Vault menu uses the new folder right away; you do not need to restart anything. Terminal: elanous onboarding # the Obsidian step asks for the vault folder Give the absolute path of the folder that contains your notes (the one with the .obsidian folder inside). A folder set from the terminal is picked up by the running daemon on the next Vault request as well — no restart. If the new path is missing or empty, elanous keeps using the vault it already had, so a mistyped path never leaves the Vault menu without notes.

In the 파일 (Files) view, the left side shows the folder tree and a breadcrumb for the current folder. The right side previews the selected file: Markdown, images and plain text. The search box searches the text of every note. Type #tag to search by tag. The 태그 (Tags) view lists every #tag in the vault, most used first. Pick one to see the notes that use it.

Open a note to edit it. The editor has a live preview next to the text. Saving is automatic. The note is saved about two and a half seconds after you stop typing. The status next to the title shows ● 편집 중 (editing), 저장 중… (saving) and ✓ 저장됨 (saved). Links. Type [[ to get suggestions from your note names. Outline and backlinks. The side panel shows the note's headings, and the other notes that link to it.

If the same note was changed on disk after you last saved it — in Obsidian, or on another device — elanous does not overwrite it silently. The editor shows a conflict message with two choices: 디스크 버전 로드 (load the disk version) — replace your text with what is on disk. 강제 덮어쓰기 (overwrite) — keep your text and write it over the disk version. The check starts when you open the note: elanous remembers the version it loaded and refuses to write over a newer one.
documents.s: When the note changed somewhere else

documents.t: Use + 새 노트 (new note) to create: an empty note with a title, a note from one of your vault templates, or today's daily note (saved under Daily/). A new note never replaces an existing one. If a note with the same name is already there, the dialog says 이미 존재하는 노트입니다 (the note already exists) and nothing is written — pick another name or open the existing note.
The 그래프 (Graph) view draws your notes as dots and their [[links]] as lines. Click a dot to open that note. Focus mode shows only the notes linked directly to the one you picked.
Obsidian vault를 찾을 수 없습니다 (vault not found) — the vault folder is not set or does not exist. Set it with elanous onboarding. The page does not load at all — see The web app (PWA).

Set up in the wizard (step 4) or edit config.json directly: "telegram": { "enabled": true, "botToken": "123456:ABC...", // from @BotFather "allowedUsers": [42, 100], // from @userinfobot — first = owner "homeChannel": -1001234567890 // optional; for cron deliveries } The bot runs inside the background service — start it with: elanous nexus run To run the poller as its own process instead, set elanous config set telegram.poller standalone and run elanous telegram run (or install it as a service with elanous telegram service --install). A bare elanous telegram only prints help. Every incoming chat+thread maps to a per-conversation session. Messages persist to the same session store as CLI chats; you can elanous session list --source telegram to audit. Replies chunk automatically at 4000 chars; parameters.retry_after on 429 is respected. Unknown user IDs (not in allowedUsers) get a polite refusal and nothing else. With an empty allowedUsers, the bot answers every sender with their user id and the command to register it (elanous config set telegram.allowedUsers '[<id>]'), and does nothing else until you do.
This walks through a real, small loop that ships in the repository: every morning, list open draft pull requests older than three days. Files: graphs/examples/stale-draft-digest/.

# graphs/examples/stale-draft-digest/stale-draft-digest.yaml graph_id: stale-draft-digest version: 1 loop: title: Stale draft PR digest trigger: { cron: "0 9 * * *" } entry_node: collect terminal_nodes: [done, failed] nodes: - { node_id: collect, kind: agent, recipe: 'cmd:collect', max_visits: 1 } - { node_id: report, kind: agent, recipe: 'cmd:report', max_visits: 1 } - { node_id: done, kind: gate, max_visits: 1 } - { node_id: failed, kind: gate, max_visits: 1 } edges: - { from: collect, on: outcome, map: { ok: report, none: done, fail: failed, error: failed } } - { from: report, on: outcome, map: { ok: done, fail: failed, error: failed } } Nodes are steps. kind says what sort of step it is (agent does work, gate checks or ends, judge decides, hitl waits for a person). Edges go by outcome. Here collect goes to report when it found something (ok) and straight to done when there was nothing (none). max_visits caps how often a step may run in one round, so a loop that goes back to fix something cannot spin forever.

# graphs/examples/stale-draft-digest/recipes.yaml collect: command: "bun graphs/examples/stale-draft-digest/digest.ts collect" timeout_ms: 60000 report: command: "bun graphs/examples/stale-draft-digest/digest.ts report" timeout_ms: 30000 A recipe is a shell command. If the last line it prints is a JSON object, that object is the step's output, and its outcome field picks the edge. A later step reads earlier outputs from the file named in ELANOUS_GRAPH_CONTEXT ({ input, outputs }) — see digest.ts.
documents.s: 2. The recipes — what each step runs

documents.t: elanous graph run graphs/examples/stale-draft-digest/stale-draft-digest.yaml --dry-run # path only elanous graph run graphs/examples/stale-draft-digest/stale-draft-digest.yaml --input '{"days":3}' # one real round Every round is saved under the state folder (graph-runs/stale-draft-digest/), and every step start and end is logged, so the round shows up in the web app's Live and Trace views.

The graph's own loop.trigger (here cron: "0 9 * * *") is the schedule: elanous loop start stale-draft-digest # preview the crontab change elanous loop start stale-draft-digest --yes # apply it elanous loop stop stale-draft-digest --yes # remove it again

Decide, don't just run — a judge step can send a round back (for example "the report is empty → collect again") within max_visits. Ask a person — a hitl step with a recipe approval: "<question>" stops the round until someone approves. Your own step kinds and sharing — a plugin can add step kinds (nodes) and ship whole loops; see Build a plugin. Package the loop in a plugin and others install it by name: elanous plugin add <plugin>@<market>.

This walks through the plugin format and the publishing tool, using a real package: video-broll, the first plugin that carries a graph. Its source folder packs/video-broll lives in the elanous source tree and is not part of the public repository; what the publisher produces from it is in elanous-plugins/video-broll.

packs/video-broll/ ├── plugin.json # Agent Plugins manifest + elanous fields └── .codex-plugin/plugin.json # Codex manifest for the same package That is all the folder holds. The skill and the graph stay where they already live in the source tree; the publisher copies them into the package (see bundle below), so there is only ever one copy to maintain.

{ "$schema": "https://antigravity.google/schemas/v1/plugin.json", "name": "video-broll", "version": "0.1.0", "description": "Cut word-timed motion B-roll into a talking-head video …", "extensions": { "ai.elanous": { "bundle": ["skills/motion-broll", { "from": "graphs/video/broll-line.yaml", "as": "graphs/broll-line.yaml" }], "graphs": ["graphs/broll-line.yaml"], "capabilities": ["fs:workdir", "proc:ffmpeg", "proc:node", "proc:python3", "agent:codex", "agent:claude"], "connectors": [], "requires": { "tools": ["ffmpeg", "node", "python3"] }, "pricing": { "model": "free" }, "category": "Productivity" } } } Field Meaning name · version · description Standard fields. name is [a-z0-9-]{2,40} and matches the folder name. A name@version is published once — it cannot be republished with different contents. bundle What to pack from the repository. A string "skills/<name>" packs that skill folder as skills/<name>/ (a lowercase skill.md is packed as SKILL.md). An object { "from": "<path>", "as": "<path in package>" } packs any file or folder. Paths resolve against --bundle-root; anything outside it — including through a symbolic link — is refused. .env files, .git/ and node_modules/ are never packed. graphs Graph files inside the package that elanous registers. Only listed graphs are registered — the loader does not scan folders. A listed graph that is not in the package stops the publish for this plugin (graph-missing). nodes Custom node kinds the plugin adds (./nodes/<kind>.yaml), registered as <plugin>:<kind> when elanous finds the installed plugin. Each node declares kind, graph (workflow or harness), inputs (a JSON Schema — the editor builds its form from it) and run — one of bash, http, skill or mcp. A node with an unknown run is skipped with a warning; the rest of the plugin still loads. capabilities What the plugin may touch, shown to the user before install: fs:workdir, net:<host>, proc:<binary>, agent:<backend>, secret:<service>. connectors Services the plugin connects to and the settings it asks the user for: { "id", "kind", "userConfig": [{ "key", "label", "secret", "env" }] }. Values are set with elanous plugin credentials or the web app and reach the plugin's graphs and servers as environment variables — named by env, or ELANOUS_PLUGIN_<PLUGIN>_<KEY> when env is absent. Fields marked secret are write-only. pricing { "model": "free" }. Only free plugins are published for now. .codex-plugin/plugin.json carries the Codex fields (name, version, description, "skills": "./skills/", interface) so Codex installs the same package.

Rule 3 is checked by the publisher today. Rules 1 and 2 describe how elanous runs plugin graphs; elanous plugin add installs plugins today, but it does not yet enforce rules 1 and 2 at install time — follow them anyway, so your plugin keeps working when it does. elanous registers only the graphs listed in graphs. When a graph runs, each step's recipe is looked up in the plugin's own recipes.yaml (next to the graph) first, then in elanous's built-in recipes. An unknown recipe is a validation error before anything runs. Third-party plugins should use their own recipes.yaml or custom nodes. If a graph uses a recipe the plugin does not ship, the publisher still publishes it but reports a warning (third-party-core-recipe). Official packs may use built-in recipes — video-broll uses the built-in broll-* steps.

elanous market keygen --out ./keys # a local test key: index-key.pem (0600) and index-key.pub.json elanous market publish --dir packs --out ./market \ --key ./keys/index-key.pem --key-id <keyId from index-key.pub.json> \ --bundle-root . # the repository root that bundle paths resolve against The output folder: Path What marketplace.json The list of plugins, written once and signed as bytes index.sig {"keyId","alg":"ed25519","sig"} over those exact bytes .agents/plugins/marketplace.json The same bytes where Codex looks for a marketplace plugins/<name>/ The unpacked package, so codex plugin marketplace add ./market can install it <name>/<version>/<sha256>.tgz The package archive; the same contents always produce the same bytes Each publish increases sequence by one. Skipped plugins are listed with a reason (paid-not-allowed-in-M0, bundle-missing, bundle-path-outside-root, graph-missing, …); warnings are listed separately. Add --json for a machine-readable result. The private key is never printed. Try the result in Codex: codex plugin marketplace add ./market codex plugin add video-broll@elanous

bun test src/market/ passes — it publishes the repository's own packs, so a new pack is checked there too. Your pack publishes with no unexpected skips or warnings. Capabilities list everything the skills and graphs touch.
documents.s: 5. Before you open a pull request

documents.t: elanous --help lists everything; elanous <command> --help shows the options of one command. This page covers the ones a user needs day to day.

Command What it does elanous start One command to begin: finds a model, starts the background service if needed and opens the web app (--tui for the terminal UI) elanous doctor Report which credentials resolve and from where, plus a readiness section (provider, gh sign-in, PATH, background service version, Linux TMPDIR) — --json for machines elanous doctor --fix / --fix --yes Show / apply the reversible repairs (the PATH block, key-cache permissions, the Linux TMPDIR block); startup files are backed up first. A missing git is offered interactively on a terminal; everything else needs --yes elanous setup Walk through missing setup steps (--non-interactive only reports) elanous login openai-codex Sign in with a ChatGPT subscription elanous login status / elanous login logout <provider> List / forget stored sign-ins elanous usage How much each account has left (subscription and credit are shown separately) elanous where Which instance this process uses, and why

Command What it does elanous harness say "<sentence>" Turn one sentence into a change: goal → worktree → tests → review → PR or branch elanous harness ask <goal.md> Same, from a goal document you wrote elanous harness plan "<sentence>" Write the plan (an RFC) without running it elanous ask "<question>" One question, one answer, new session elanous chat "<message>" One message in the current session elanous agent "<task>" One turn with file and shell tools elanous repl Multi-turn session in the shell elanous The terminal UI Useful harness say / harness ask options: --dry-run (plan only), --no-auto-merge (leave the PR for you), --target <dir> (work on another directory), --child-llm-provider <id> --child-llm-model <id> (pick the model that writes the code).

Command What it does elanous logs --since 30m Logs from every surface; filter with --category, --event, --grep elanous harness worktrees Worktrees the harness made, and whether each is safe to remove elanous harness clean Remove finished harness worktrees (dry run unless --yes; open PRs are always kept) elanous ops status What the autonomous parts are doing right now

Command What it does elanous tasks list / elanous tasks approve <id> See queued tasks / approve one that came from outside elanous card list / elanous card show <id> Tasks as cards, and one card with its sections elanous directive add "<instruction>" --dry-run Preview an instruction as a Linear issue; drop --dry-run to create it elanous loop list / status / run Loop agents — see Loop agents elanous plugin add / list / remove Install and manage plugins — see Plugins

Command What it does elanous config get [path] / elanous config set <path> <value> Read / change settings (secrets are hidden) elanous config path Which config file is active elanous provider The active model provider, model and sign-in state elanous tier Which model each tier (budget … best) maps to per provider

Command What it does elanous nexus run Start the service (web app, chat bots, remote control) elanous nexus status / elanous nexus stop Check / stop it elanous nexus install --launchd (macOS) · --systemd-user (Linux) Run it at login; API keys are read from the key cache, not written into the service file elanous nexus build Build the web app (from a checkout — see install) elanous nexus restart-needed Say whether the running service needs a restart, only a web-app build, or nothing (exit 0 none · 10 build · 11 restart · 2 unknown) elanous update [--restart] Update to the latest release (--version <v> for a specific one; from a checkout, reinstall that checkout); restart the service only if it is needed and you passed --restart. Same as self-update. elanous update --auto on updates daily
When you make an HTML page with elanous — a report, a note, a diagram, a site draft — this guide puts it at a public address in a few minutes. It uses Vercel, a hosting service with a free plan.
documents.s: Put an HTML page on the web with Vercel

documents.t: Create an account at vercel.com. The free Hobby plan is for personal, non-commercial use; use a paid plan for business sites. Install the command-line tool and sign in: npm i -g vercel vercel login

Put the page and everything it uses (images, CSS) in one folder, with the main file named index.html. Then: cd my-page vercel deploy --prod The first time, answer the questions (project name, scope). Vercel prints the address, for example https://my-page.vercel.app.
Change the files and run vercel deploy --prod again in the same folder. The address stays the same.

Want Do A preview address before going live vercel deploy (without --prod) Your own domain Vercel dashboard → Project → Settings → Domains Keep it out of search engines Add <meta name="robots" content="noindex"> to the page
A deployed page is public. Do not put passwords, keys, personal data or private documents in the folder. Check that you have the right to publish every image and text in it.

When elanous builds a web page for you, it follows the design system chosen for the project. A design system is a set of files: a DESIGN.md that describes the look, and a tokens.css holding the actual colours, fonts and spacing. elanous measures the result against those same files. You can also start from a site you like: elanous measures it and builds a new site in a similar concept (web clone). Everything here works out of the box, except full preview pages. Those need OpenDesign, a separate, free program. See OpenDesign (optional).

What it is 52 design systems Style-based systems (Modern & Minimal, Bold & Expressive, Retro, Professional, …) imported from OpenDesign's catalogue under Apache-2.0. Systems named after companies or products are left out, so no one else's brand goes into your project. 6 terminal themes Colour directions for terminal-style projects. 13 craft rulebooks Rules the build agent follows: anti-AI-slop, accessibility, colour, typography, motion, forms, state coverage, laws of UX, right-to-left text. A measurer and a gate They check a page against the chosen system. Neither calls a model. These are plain files that travel inside the elanous package. They need no network, no account and no extra program.

In the PWA, open Design check (/design-check). Every system is shown as a card with its colours, fonts, category and a one-line mood. Press Select on a card. You can switch to another system later. From the terminal: elanous repo design-direction <project> # list systems and themes elanous repo design-direction <project> --set paper # choose one Choosing a system writes three things into the project: design/system/DESIGN.md and design/system/tokens.css, copied as they are. A ## Design direction section in the project's DESIGN.md naming the system, the tokens file and its source. If you edited the copied files by hand, elanous will not overwrite them when you switch systems. It says which file is in the way instead. From then on, agents that build pages in this project read DESIGN.md and use the tokens (var(--fg), var(--font-display), …) instead of inventing colours.

elanous repo design-lint <page.html> # one page: AI-default smells and token use elanous repo design-gate <project> # the whole project: pass / fail design-gate finds the HTML files in the project and measures each one against the chosen system. It reports one of three verdicts: pass fail, when there is at least one serious finding, such as a serif system being given a hard-coded sans-serif heading not applicable, when no system is chosen or the project has no HTML Exit codes are 0 for pass or not applicable, 1 for fail and 2 when the check could not run. The last line of output is JSON, so scripts can read the verdict. A rule the gate could not check is listed as not checked. It is never counted as passed.
documents.s: Check that a page follows it

documents.t: elanous can study a live site and help you build a new site in a similar concept. It measures what the browser actually drew, turns that into a DESIGN.md, and then builds and checks against it like any other system. elanous repo design-extract https://example.com --no-assets --out ./ref # the look, in seconds elanous repo design-css ./ref/<site>/DESIGN.md # turn it into tokens.css design-extract opens the page in Chrome and records: the site's CSS custom properties the colours really painted, ranked by how much they are used font sizes and weights by role, and the type scale spacing steps, line length and motion It writes these into a DESIGN.md in the format elanous reads. A value it could not read is marked as unread, never guessed. How long it takes, measured on a laptop: Run Time Output design-extract --no-assets (the look only) 5–6 seconds per site DESIGN.md + tokens.json design-extract --viewports 390,768,1280 (with images and three widths) about 3 minutes for a large marketing site ~300 files, ~90 MB design-archive (the whole original, following several pages) more than 4 minutes on a large site the original HTML, CSS, JS and assets, indexed What you get depends on the site: Site What design-extract returns Uses CSS custom properties Named tokens (hundreds on a large site), plus measured values Plain CSS without custom properties No named tokens, but measured painted colours, type roles and spacing Put the result in your project's DESIGN.md. design-lint and design-gate then measure against it, the same way they do for a bundled system. Ask the harness to build the new site from it — for example elanous harness say "target paths: index.html · styles.css — a landing page for <your product> following DESIGN.md". design-archive keeps the original locally. Uploading it needs a private bucket: elanous checks that the bucket is not public first and refuses when it cannot tell. Reference, not a copy Use a site to learn its rhythm, palette and proportions. Do not ship another company's logo, name, images or text as your own. Needs: Chrome (or Chromium/Edge). See Recommended programs.
documents.s: Rebuild a site you like — web clone

documents.t: OpenDesign is a free, open-source (Apache-2.0) design tool. elanous uses it for one thing: drawing preview pages. You give it one brief, for example "a coffee subscription landing page", and it draws a full page in each candidate system. You then see real screens side by side before you choose. Without OpenDesign, everything above still works; you choose from the cards instead of from full previews.

Docker (Compose v2) The official image ghcr.io/nexu-io/od. Its default memory limit is 384 MB. On a Mac, Docker Desktop's VM needs more than that. An engine to draw with This is where cost can come in. OpenDesign itself is free, but each preview is drawn by a model: either a coding-agent CLI you already subscribe to (Codex, Claude Code), or a provider API key such as OPENAI_API_KEY (billed per use). The Docker image does not include the agent CLIs. On Linux you can mount the ones installed on the host; otherwise use an API key. Time Around four minutes per preview in our tests. Running from source (Node 24 and pnpm) works too. It used about 730 MB in development mode in our tests.

Start OpenDesign with an API token set (OD_API_TOKEN in its .env). Save the token in a file readable only by you (chmod 600). Tell elanous where to find OpenDesign and the token: elanous config set design.openDesign.url http://<host>:7456 elanous config set design.openDesign.tokenFile ~/.config/open-design/api-token Then draw previews: elanous repo design-preview <project> --brief "A coffee subscription landing page" \ --systems minimal,paper --agent codex Previews are saved to design/previews/<system>.html. In the PWA's Design check, a card that has a preview shows a Preview button. The page opens in a sandboxed frame, so its scripts do not run, and you can choose the system from there. If OpenDesign is not set up, design-preview stops and says which two settings are missing. Nothing else changes. Keep the token OpenDesign does not ask for a token when a request comes from the machine it runs on. Do not publish it through a proxy on that machine, for example tailscale serve. Bind it to a private network address and keep OD_API_TOKEN set.
